l: the land, The Book of Helaman
s: The land extends from the sea west to the sea east. It experiences great famine, exceedingly great peace, war, dryness, destruction, and a curse because of wickedness and abominations. It has no light for three days when Jesus Christ suffers death, then receives rain, brings forth fruit and grain, and its people rebuild and spread across it.

l: covenant of secrecy, The Book of Helaman
s: The band of Kishkumen had entered into a covenant that no one should know its wickedness.

l: secret work of murder and robbery, The Book of Helaman
s: Secret works of darkness center on Gadianton’s murder-and-robbery band and judges angered when Nephi exposes their secret practices.

l: plan to murder Helaman, The Book of Helaman
s: Kishkumen planned to murder Helaman in order to destroy him. Helaman's servant learned of the plan through disguise and prevented it by killing Kishkumen.

l: the secret band of Gadianton, The Book of Helaman
s: The secret band of Gadianton is a secret combination to murder, rob, and gain power. Established by Gadianton the robber in the more settled parts of the land, it persists because government leaders do not know of it. It includes judges and a judge’s murderer, and its authors are Gadianton and the evil one.

l: murder of Kishkumen, The Book of Helaman
s: is_a stabbing [to the heart, causing death] Helaman's servant stabbed Kishkumen even to the heart as they went toward the judgment-seat, and Kishkumen fell dead without a groan.

l: flight of Gadianton's band, The Book of Helaman
s: is_a flight [out of the land by a secret way into the wilderness] When Gadianton learned that Kishkumen had not returned, he caused his band to follow him. They fled out of the land by a secret way into the wilderness and could not be found.

l: the law, The Book of Helaman
s: is_a law [corrupt] Nephi speaks concerning the corruptness of the law. The judges accuse him of reviling against the people and their law.

l: the reign of the judges, The Book of Helaman
s: The reign of the judges over the people of Nephi spans years of contention, wars, prosperity, peace, and pride, including Helaman’s death and Nephi’s succession, and continues through the ninetieth year.

l: overthrow and near-destruction of the people of Nephi, The Book of Helaman
s: affects people (people of Nephi) [almost the entire destruction] The text states that Gadianton would prove the overthrow, almost the entire destruction, of the people of Nephi.

l: church of God, The Book of Helaman
s: The church of God is a church that receives many souls baptized unto repentance and first experiences exceedingly great prosperity. Pride among some who profess to belong to it brings persecution, though the church itself is distinguished from their pride. It then dwindles because of iniquity, including denial of prophecy and revelation. Later it is established among the Lamanites and spreads throughout the land, with most Nephites and Lamanites belonging to it amid exceedingly great peace.

l: Nephi, The Book of Helaman
s: Nephi is Helaman’s eldest son, a judge, prophet, preacher, and servant of God. After Helaman dies, he succeeds him in the judgment-seat and governs with justice and equity, keeping God’s commandments. With Lehi, he warns the Nephites about their iniquities and the consequences of refusing repentance. Wearied by the people’s wickedness, he gives the judgment-seat to Cezoram and devotes the rest of his days to preaching, prophesying, baptizing, and declaring repentance among Nephites and Lamanites. Imprisoned with Lehi, he is encircled by fire without being burned. After preaching and prophesying in the land northward, where his words are rejected, he returns to Zarahemla mourning for the Nephites. From his garden and tower, he prays to God, condemns corrupt law and secret works of darkness, and testifies of approaching judgments and destruction unless the people repent. Though accused of murdering Seezoram, he reveals Seantum as the murderer and is released after Seantum confesses. God blesses Nephi for his unwearying declaration of the word; when people seek to imprison him, the Spirit conveys him away. He continues among all the people, performing signs, wonders, miracles, prophecy, preaching, and baptism for those who confess their sins.

l: God, The Book of Helaman
s: God is the holy God and the people's God, source of heavenly authority, mercy, judgment, knowledge, and power. He opens heaven to those who believe on Jesus Christ, receives souls in the kingdom of heaven, and is merciful to all who sincerely call on his holy name; those who yield their hearts receive purification and sanctification. He gives people knowledge of good and evil and free agency to choose good or evil, life or death. God works through prophets and servants: he was with holy prophets, gave Moses power, revealed destruction to Nephi, commanded and blessed Nephi, made him mighty, and granted him power over the people, including power whose earthly sealing or loosing is effective in heaven. God sends angels, the Holy Spirit, and a voice from above darkness to call people to repentance. He displays power through fire, earthquakes, darkness, famine, rain, and fruitful land. The wicked Nephites reject his word, rebel, harden their hearts, and seek to destroy his servants; God is angered and will not show them strength unless they repent and hearken. After their repentance, he turns away anger, sends rain, and restores fruit and grain. God chastens because he loves, promises mercy and latter-time blessings to the afflicted, scattered Lamanites, and will not utterly destroy them in his wisdom. Yet he requires the people of Nephi to repent and observe his will, warning that he will utterly destroy them if they do not.

l: Abraham, The Book of Helaman
s: sees the coming of Christ [with gladness] Abraham saw of the coming of the Son of God, was filled with gladness, and rejoiced. He was among those who knew of these things.

l: the evil one, The Book of Helaman
s: The evil one is one whose words the children of men are quick to heed, leading them to set their hearts upon the vain things of the world. The unbelievers accused Samuel of having a devil, claiming that the devil's power prevented them from hitting him.

l: land southward, The Book of Helaman
s: is_possessed_by Nephites [before Lamanite conquest] Dissenters from the Nephites, assisted by the Lamanites, obtained all the possession of the Nephites that was in the land southward.

l: earth, The Book of Helaman
s: The earth obeys the Lord’s command: it moves backward to lengthen the day, rather than the sun. It is shaken and rocked; rocks, mountains, valleys, highways, and cities are broken or changed, while scattering occurs across its face.

l: kingdom of heaven, The Book of Helaman
s: receives immortal souls [at the right hand of God] The kingdom of heaven is described as the place where the souls of the faithful may sit with Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and the holy fathers.

l: word of the Lord, The Book of Helaman
s: The word of the Lord is a quick and powerful word of God that can divide the devil’s cunning, snares, and wiles and lead the man of Christ in a strait and narrow course. Nephi and Lehi preach it among the people of Nephi and the Lamanites with power and authority. It commands repentance to avoid destruction, is declared by prophets including Samuel to testify of sins, and is often rejected when it condemns deeds. It is also taught by those on whom the people depend, raising fears of ignorance.

l: migration to the land northward, The Book of Helaman
s: is_a movement of people [from Zarahemla to the land northward] An exceedingly great many people depart from Zarahemla and travel northward to inherit the land. They spread across the land and establish cities and settlements.

l: baptism unto repentance, The Book of Helaman
s: Baptism unto repentance unites many souls to the church of God: during prosperity tens of thousands join, dissenters confess sins before returning to the Nephites, and eight thousand Lamanites in Zarahemla and nearby regions are received.

l: repentance, The Book of Helaman
s: Repentance is a condition of baptism, a repeated command to turn unto the Lord, and the path by which people receive salvation, remission of sins, and redemption through the power and merits of Jesus Christ. It is joined with faith, humility, hearkening to the Lord, confession of sins, and a change of heart. As the church grows, people are baptized unto repentance and united to the church of God. The Nephites repent after preaching by Moronihah, Nephi, and Lehi; they prosper and regain possessions and lands. Repentance is preached to Lamanites and Nephites, bringing many into humility as followers of God and the Lamb. Warnings repeatedly contrast repentance with destruction: those who repent and hearken receive the Lord God's strength, are blessed, and may be saved, while those who refuse lose cities, lands, salvation, and are destroyed. When famine and destruction threaten, the people humble themselves in sackcloth; Nephi prays, and the Lord turns away his anger. Repentance and returning to the Lord can thus spare the people, prevent everlasting destruction, and keep them from being cast into the fire. In the end, Nephi preaches repentance, and believers in Samuel's words repent and confess their sins.

l: prosperity, The Book of Helaman
s: blesses church of God [exceedingly great] The church experiences exceedingly great prosperity in the forty-ninth year, bringing thousands into the church and causing even the high priests and teachers to be astonished.

l: peace, The Book of Helaman
s: Peace is established in the land in the forty-ninth year, continuing through later years as people travel, trade, prosper, rebuild, and the church spreads. It persists despite pride, famine, and doctrinal contentions, but eventually ends as wickedness, secret murders, and strife arise.

l: joy, The Book of Helaman
s: is_present_in land of Zarahemla [continual rejoicing] The people experience continual rejoicing, exceedingly great joy, and great joy during the forty-ninth and fiftieth years.

l: pride, The Book of Helaman
s: Pride begins with little dissensions, grows through riches and prosperity, enters professing church members’ hearts, causes persecution of many brethren, and remains among most people by the eighty-seventh year.

l: persecution, The Book of Helaman
s: causes affliction [among the more humble people] People lifted up in pride persecute many of their brethren. The more humble part of the people suffers great persecutions and affliction but grows stronger in humility and faith.

l: faith of Christ, The Book of Helaman
s: is_strengthened_by fasting and prayer [among the more humble people] The humble people fast and pray often and become firmer in the faith of Christ. Their faith contributes to joy, consolation, purification, and sanctification.

l: righteousness, The Book of Helaman
s: is_in the Lord [as the nature of the Eternal Head] The righteousness of the Lamanites exceeds that of the Nephites because of their firmness and steadiness in the faith. The Nephites turn from righteousness and trample God’s commandments.

l: murder, The Book of Helaman
s: Secret murders are committed by Gadianton’s bands to obtain gain. The Nephites join in secret murders and combinations, and Cezoram and his son are murdered in the judgment-seat.

l: death of Helaman, The Book of Helaman
s: occurs_in fifty and third year [of the reign of the judges] Helaman dies in the fifty-third year of the reign of the judges, after governing with justice and equity and raising Nephi and Lehi.

l: succession of Nephi, The Book of Helaman
s: follows death of Helaman [Nephi begins to reign in Helaman's stead] After Helaman's death, his eldest son Nephi begins to reign in his stead and takes the judgment-seat.

l: dissenters, The Book of Helaman
s: Dissenters, a group from the Nephites, go to the Lamanites and stir them to war, helping a numerous Lamanite army obtain Nephite possessions in the land southward. Later, Nephi and Lehi’s preaching confounds many dissenters; they confess sins, are baptized unto repentance, return to the Nephites, and repair their wrongs.

l: armies of Moronihah, The Book of Helaman
s: Armies driven to Bountiful fortify a sea-to-sea line, regain many cities and half the Nephites’ possessions, then defend recovered lands.

l: war between the Nephites and Lamanites, The Book of Helaman
s: A war sparked by dissenters brings bloodshed; Lamanites gain lands, and Nephites recover half their possessions but advance no further.

l: slaughter of the Nephites, The Book of Helaman
s: A slaughter among the Nephites, caused by wickedness, iniquity, abomination, pride, oppression, violence, and disbelief.

l: loss of the Nephites, The Book of Helaman
s: A great loss caused by wickedness and abomination: the Nephites lose almost all lands, repent, then regain half.

l: riches, The Book of Helaman
s: Riches bring the Nephites and Lamanites abundance through metals, grain, flocks, herds, and cloth. The Nephites set their hearts on them, seek elevation over one another, and remember them instead of the Lord; riches cause pride, are cursed, and become slippery.

l: spirit of prophecy, The Book of Helaman
s: is_disbelieved_in_by Nephites [because of iniquity] The Nephites began to disbelieve in the spirit of prophecy, and some who professed to belong to the church of God denied it.

l: spirit of revelation, The Book of Helaman
s: is_disbelieved_in_by Nephites [because of iniquity] The Nephites began to disbelieve in the spirit of revelation, and some who professed to belong to the church of God denied it.

l: the Spirit of the Lord, The Book of Helaman
s: The Spirit of the Lord does not dwell in unholy temples and withdraws from the weak, wicked, hard-hearted Nephites, no longer preserving them. After darkness disperses, the Holy Spirit of God enters people’s hearts, filling them as with fire and enabling marvelous words. It is poured out upon believing Lamanites, conveys Nephi away from the people, and is with Samuel, preventing stones and arrows from striking him.

l: laws of Mosiah, The Book of Helaman
s: Laws given to the people by the Lord’s commandment, later altered and trampled by Nephites, contributing to their wickedness.

l: the commandments of God, The Book of Helaman
s: The commandments of God are given by the Lord and taught by Helaman as obligations for people to remember and keep. Nephi and Lehi keep them while teaching the word of God. Yet the Nephites set them at naught, turn away, and trample them underfoot, replacing obedience with their own ways and idols; increasing disobedience brings wickedness and weakness.

l: judgments of God, The Book of Helaman
s: Judgments of God confront the wicked, disbelieving Nephites and stand at the people’s doors, coming upon them unless they repent.

l: miraculous and matchless power of the Lord, The Book of Helaman
s: preserves Nephites [before their unbelief and wickedness] The Lord ceased to preserve the Nephites by his miraculous and matchless power because they had fallen into unbelief and awful wickedness.

l: Aminadab, The Book of Helaman
s: Aminadab, a Nephite by birth and former church member, dissents from the Nephites, recognizes Nephi and Lehi with angels, and urges Lamanites to repent, gain faith in Christ, and follow teachings of Jesus Christ.

l: angels of God, The Book of Helaman
s: Angels of God minister to Nephi in prison, Lamanites after the heavens open, and about three hundred souls; they appear to wise men and declare glad tidings of great joy.

l: eternal life, The Book of Helaman
s: Eternal life is a precious, unfading heavenly gift. Helaman teaches that doing good without boasting lays up this treasure; those who look upon the Son of God with faith and a contrite spirit may receive it, and it is promised to those who have done good.

l: atoning blood of Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman
s: is_the_only_way_to salvation [for mankind] Helaman teaches that there is no other way or means whereby people can be saved except through the atoning blood of Jesus Christ, who comes to redeem the world.

l: rock of our Redeemer, The Book of Helaman
s: Helaman teaches that Jesus Christ, the Son of God, is the sure foundation; those who build on this rock cannot fall despite the devil’s storms.

l: prison, The Book of Helaman
s: A prison in the land of Nephi holds Nephi and Lehi after capture; it shakes, is surrounded by fire, and remains standing during manifestations.

l: pillar of fire, The Book of Helaman
s: A pillar of fire encircles Nephi and Lehi, then every soul, protecting them and the prison without causing harm.

l: cloud of darkness, The Book of Helaman
s: A cloud of darkness overshadows imprisoned Lamanites, causing fear and preventing flight, then disperses after their repentance and cry to the voice.

l: voice, The Book of Helaman
s: A voice from above darkness commands imprisoned people to repent and stop destroying God’s servants, pierces their souls in mildness, then speaks peace through faith in the Well Beloved.

l: earthquake, The Book of Helaman
s: shakes prison [repeatedly while the voice speaks] The earth shakes exceedingly when Nephi and Lehi speak, when the voice commands repentance, and when marvelous words are spoken. The shaking occurs repeatedly while the prison walls tremble but do not fall.

l: preaching, The Book of Helaman
s: Preaching unfolds as Nephi and Lehi travel among Nephites and Lamanites, confound dissenters, convert many Lamanites, and call people to repentance alongside Samuel’s prophecy.

l: Jerusalem, The Book of Helaman
s: Jerusalem is a place destroyed according to Jeremiah’s words; Lehi was driven out after testifying of Christ, who would show himself there.

l: traditions of their fathers, The Book of Helaman
s: Traditions of their fathers are exposed as wicked, causing Lamanite iniquity and unbelief. Lamanites are convinced through repentance and spiritual evidences, abandon the traditions after conversion, and come to belief.

l: the people of the church, The Book of Helaman
s: has_joy great joy [because of the conversion of the Lamanites and the church of God] The people of the church have great joy because of the conversion of the Lamanites and fellowship and rejoice with one another.

l: the Lord, The Book of Helaman
s: The Lord is a creator and divine ruler concerned with the welfare, happiness, and salvation of the children of men. He shows goodness and mercy, blesses and prospers those who trust him, protects them from enemies, and pours out his Spirit on those willing to believe his words. He also chastens wickedness and hardness of heart through death, terror, famine, pestilence, and other afflictions, and can command the earth and its elements. He calls people to repent so they may be saved, sends Samuel by an angel to warn and prophesy to the Nephites, promises to spare repentant people, and is the one to whom people seek baptism.

l: Satan, The Book of Helaman
s: Satan is the author of sin who inspires secret murder and preserves wicked plots, oaths, covenants, and plans across generations. He stirs Nephites to join robber bands, continually incites iniquity, spreads rumors and contention, and hardens people’s hearts against what is good and what should come.

l: Gadianton’s robbers and murderers, The Book of Helaman
s: Gadianton’s robbers and murderers are a band of robbers and murderers using secret signs and words to identify covenant brothers. They murder Cezoram and his son in the judgment-seat without being found. Though the Lamanites hunt and destroy the band among themselves, the Nephites build it up; it fills judgment-seats, usurps authority, abandons God’s commandments, and pursues gain, glory, and wicked rule.

l: faith, The Book of Helaman
s: Faith in Christ brings a change of heart and repentance, supports refusing violence, and makes Lamanites righteous, firm, and steadfast. They believe God’s words, preach faith to Nephites, gain truth through scriptures, and fear taking up buried weapons.

l: secret oaths and covenants, The Book of Helaman
s: Secret oaths and covenants bind robbers and murderers to avoid punishment for wickedness; Alma commands their concealment because revealing and spreading them could bring destruction.

l: destruction, The Book of Helaman
s: Destruction is an imminent, heavy, and certain fate awaiting the Nephites unless they repent. Their murders, fornication, wickedness, oppression, abominations, and rejection of the Lord ripen them for everlasting destruction. Secret oaths, covenants, and bands of robbers help bring it about. It is foretold that their cities and lands will be taken and that they will be destroyed from the earth. It begins through robbers and the sword, grows severe through famine, and includes killings and captivity among Nephites and Lamanites.

l: the judges, The Book of Helaman
s: The judges are men in the secret band of Gadianton with corrupt law. Angry with Nephi, they accuse him of arranging Seezoram’s murder but fear the people and do not seize him. At Seezoram’s burial they question five men, bring Nephi before the multitude, then learn through Seantum’s confession that Nephi was not the murderer.

l: garden of Nephi, The Book of Helaman
s: is_location_of Nephi [the judges heard his words there] The garden of Nephi is where the judges hear Nephi’s words before gathering at the burial of the chief judge.

l: the righteous, The Book of Helaman
s: The righteous preserve Zarahemla; the Lord spares repentant people, but destruction follows if the righteous are cast out.

l: Nephi's mourning, The Book of Helaman
s: Nephi's mourning, caused by sorrow over the people's iniquities, unfolds on his tower as he pours out his soul unto God, gathers multitudes, and preaches repentance.

l: iniquity, The Book of Helaman
s: Iniquity brings curses upon the land and riches, opposes righteousness by seeking happiness through wrongdoing, and causes spiritual death without repentance. People are called to repent through the merits of Jesus Christ. The Lord chastens the people of Nephi in their iniquities, while inherited traditions drive Lamanite evil deeds. Most people remain wicked and increase in iniquity.

l: Moses, The Book of Helaman
s: Moses, a man with great power from God, divided the Red Sea, testified of the Messiah’s coming, and lifted up the brazen serpent as his likeness.

l: the holy prophets, The Book of Helaman
s: The holy prophets, from the days of Moses and Abraham through Nephi, testify of the Messiah, Christ’s coming, sins, and iniquities, with prophecies written in holy scriptures. People cast out, mock, stone, and kill them, later regretting ignored warnings. Their words begin to be fulfilled in the ninetieth year.

l: redemption, The Book of Helaman
s: comes_to the people [through the order of God's Son] Redemption was to come to the people through the Son of God. Abraham and others knew of these things, and the people were shown them many thousand years before his coming.

l: the destruction of Jerusalem, The Book of Helaman
s: is_testified_of_by Jeremiah The destruction of Jerusalem occurred according to Jeremiah's words. Nephi uses it as evidence that the Son of God will come according to prophecy.

l: the day of judgment, The Book of Helaman
s: is_a day The people are heaping up wrath against the day of judgment instead of laying up treasures in heaven. Their murders, fornication, and wickedness are ripening them for destruction.

l: treasures, The Book of Helaman
s: Treasures hidden in the earth by the righteous are concealed; others hide them while fleeing enemies and lose them, and the wicked cannot find them because of the land’s curse.

l: Seezoram, The Book of Helaman
s: Seezoram, chief judge, is found dead at the judgment-seat, murdered by his brother Seantum; his death confirms the miracle Nephi foretold.

l: Seantum, The Book of Helaman
s: Seantum, Seezoram’s brother, murders him, denies it when questioned, then is exposed by blood on his cloak and confesses.

l: five men, The Book of Helaman
s: Five men verify Nephi’s prophecy, find Seezoram dead, are imprisoned as suspected murderers, convert in prison, and are released after confirmation.

l: murder of Seezoram, The Book of Helaman
s: is_committed_by Seantum [Seantum is his brother] The murder of Seezoram is committed by his brother Seantum, who stabs him under a garb of secrecy. Nephi predicts how Seantum’s guilt will be exposed, and Seantum confesses.

l: burial of the chief judge, The Book of Helaman
s: The people assemble to mourn and fast at slain chief judge Seezoram’s burial; judges and five men are involved, and the five men are released that day.

l: Nephi's prophecy, The Book of Helaman
s: concerns Seezoram [his death as chief judge] Nephi’s prophecy that the chief judge would be dead is confirmed when the five men find Seezoram’s body. Nephi also prophesies the questioning, signs of guilt, and confession of Seantum, and these details occur as he described.

l: people (scattered multitudes), The Book of Helaman
s: The scattered multitudes reject Nephi’s warning of destruction unless they repent, harden their hearts, seek to imprison Nephi, become divided, and slay one another with the sword.

l: division among the people, The Book of Helaman
s: is_a division A division arises among the people, causing them to divide hither and thither and leave Nephi alone.

l: Nephi's power, The Book of Helaman
s: A power given by God to Nephi, enabling sealing and loosing on earth and in heaven, declarations of smiting, famine, and destruction according to the Lord’s will, and escape through the Spirit from imprisonment.

l: famine, The Book of Helaman
s: Famine is a punishment Nephi may bring upon the land for wickedness. After his prayer, a great famine causes many to perish and remember the Lord; when the people repent, the Lord sends rain and it ceases.

l: destruction of the people, The Book of Helaman
s: The Lord declares through Nephi that the people will be smitten unto destruction unless they repent. Nephi repeatedly declares this warning to the people.

l: death of the chief judge, The Book of Helaman
s: is_a great miracle [performed by Nephi] The people had previously been told by Nephi about the death of the chief judge, but even that great miracle did not cause them to hearken to the words of the Lord.

l: slaying with the sword, The Book of Helaman
s: is_a violence [among the people] As contentions increase, the people become divided against themselves and begin to slay one another with the sword.

l: Nephi, The Book of Helaman
s: Nephi, Lehi’s brother, is a great prophet and man of God with God-given power and authority, receiving daily revelations. He prays for famine to avert sword destruction, then prays for it to end when the people repent and esteem him.

l: the children of men, The Book of Helaman
s: The children of men are an unsteady group, less than the dust of the earth. They quickly do iniquity, heed the evil one, pursue vain things, and rise in pride, while slowly doing good, remembering the Lord their God, hearing his counsels, and walking in wisdom’s paths; they reject him as ruler and guide.

l: the dust of the earth, The Book of Helaman
s: moves hither and thither [at the command of God] The dust of the earth moves hither and thither at the command of the great and everlasting God. It is used as a comparison showing that the children of men are less than it.

l: good works, The Book of Helaman
s: restores_to grace [grace for grace, according to works] Good works are sought for men to be brought unto repentance and restored unto grace for grace according to their works.

l: the great and last day, The Book of Helaman
s: is_a time of judgment In the great and last day, some will be cast out and cast off from the presence of the Lord.

l: endless misery, The Book of Helaman
s: is_a state [to which some are consigned] Endless misery is the state to which some who are cast off from the presence of the Lord will be consigned.

l: everlasting damnation, The Book of Helaman
s: is_received_by those that have done evil Everlasting damnation is the consequence stated for those who have done evil.

l: an angel of the Lord, The Book of Helaman
s: An angel of the Lord declares Jesus Christ’s coming to Samuel, commands repentance, and reveals signs accompanying Christ’s death.

l: the sword of justice, The Book of Helaman
s: hangs_over the Nephites [until four hundred years pass] The sword of justice hangs over the Nephites. The Lord declares that it will fall upon them within four hundred years unless they repent.

l: faith on the Lord Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman
s: saves_from destruction [with repentance] Faith on the Lord Jesus Christ is identified with repentance as the means by which the people can be saved from the destruction that awaits them.

l: the suffering and death of Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman
s: is_for the people At the death of Jesus Christ, the sun, moon, and stars shall give no light for three days. Thunderings, lightnings, earthquakes, tempests, broken rocks, changed landscapes, and opened graves shall accompany his death.

l: the curse of the land, The Book of Helaman
s: The curse of the land comes upon wicked, abominable people, making hidden treasures, riches, tools, and swords slippery and unavailable to them.

l: salvation, The Book of Helaman
s: Salvation is delayed by procrastination until it is everlastingly too late, depends on repentance and faith on the Lord Jesus Christ, and comes through the death of Jesus Christ. Those who believe on the Son of God may be saved; it comes to the Lamanites through Nephite preaching.

l: believers in the Son of God, The Book of Helaman
s: have everlasting life Believers in the Son of God shall have everlasting life. Those who believe on his name may be saved.

l: the unrepentant, The Book of Helaman
s: are_cast_into fire The unrepentant are hewn down and cast into the fire. They suffer a second spiritual death and bring condemnation upon themselves.

l: the presence of the Lord, The Book of Helaman
s: The fall of Adam cuts all mankind off from the presence of the Lord, and the resurrection of Christ brings mankind back into that presence.

l: the sign of Christ’s coming, The Book of Helaman
s: The sign of Christ’s coming includes great lights in heaven, a darknessless night before he is born, a new star, and many signs and wonders in heaven.

l: the birth of Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman
s: The night before Jesus Christ is born shall not be dark, and it shall appear as if it were day. A new star shall arise as a sign of his birth.

l: the resurrection of Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman
s: The resurrection of Jesus Christ redeems all mankind, brings them into the Lord’s presence, and brings to pass repentance.

l: spiritual death, The Book of Helaman
s: Spiritual death is separation from the Lord: first through Adam’s fall, cutting mankind from His presence; second upon those who do not repent, cut off from righteousness.

l: the fall of Adam, The Book of Helaman
s: causes spiritual death [by cutting mankind off from the presence of the Lord] The fall of Adam cuts all mankind off from the presence of the Lord, leaving them considered dead in temporal and spiritual things.

l: the darknessless night, The Book of Helaman
s: is_a the sign of Christ’s coming [the night before Jesus Christ is born] The night before Jesus Christ is born shall have no darkness and shall appear to people as if it were day.

l: the new star, The Book of Helaman
s: is_a the sign of Christ’s coming [a star never before seen] A new star shall arise as a sign of the birth of Jesus Christ, unlike any star previously seen.

l: signs and wonders, The Book of Helaman
s: Signs and wonders amaze Nephi’s people, causing them to fall; they are warned to repent and taught that Christ must shortly come.

l: the darkening of the sun, moon, and stars, The Book of Helaman
s: is_a_sign_of the death of Jesus Christ [lasting three days] At the death of Jesus Christ, the sun shall be darkened and refuse to give its light, and the moon and stars shall also give no light for three days.

l: thunderings and lightnings, The Book of Helaman
s: Thunderings and lightnings accompany Jesus Christ yielding up the ghost and the earthquake for many hours.

l: the earthquake, The Book of Helaman
s: shakes the earth [when Jesus Christ yields up the ghost] The earth shall shake and tremble when Jesus Christ yields up the ghost.

l: the tempests, The Book of Helaman
s: cover the earth [during the darkness] Great tempests shall occur during the signs accompanying the death of Jesus Christ, while darkness covers the whole earth for three days.

l: good and evil, The Book of Helaman
s: are_distinguishable the children of men [through knowledge given by God] God gives people knowledge to distinguish good from evil. People may choose good and be restored to good, or choose evil and have evil restored to them.

l: free agency, The Book of Helaman
s: permits the people [to act for themselves] People are free and permitted to act for themselves. They may choose life or death and bring upon themselves the consequences of their choices.

l: life or death, The Book of Helaman
s: is_a_choice_for the people [according to their actions] People are given the choice of life or death. They can choose good and be restored to good, or choose evil and have evil restored to them.

l: mighty works, The Book of Helaman
s: Mighty works have been shown to the people of Nephi. The Lord says the Lamanites who dwindled in unbelief would not have done so again if those mighty works had been shown to them.

l: unbelief, The Book of Helaman
s: causes dwindling [among those affected by ancestral traditions] The Lamanites may dwindle in unbelief, but the Lord will prolong their days until the promised restoration. The people of Nephi face utter destruction because of their unbelief despite the mighty works done among them.

l: knowledge of the truth, The Book of Helaman
s: leads_to faith [through belief in holy scriptures and prophetic writings] The Lamanites who are brought to knowledge of the truth and learn of the wicked traditions of their fathers are led to believe the holy scriptures, have faith and repentance, and experience a change of heart. The Lamanites are promised restoration to knowledge of the truth.

l: prophecies, The Book of Helaman
s: Samuel and Nephi prophesied, and the words of the prophets began to be fulfilled.

l: restoration of the Lamanites, The Book of Helaman
s: is_prophesied knowledge of the truth [by fathers, Zenos, and many other prophets] The restoration of the Lamanites is prophesied as their return to knowledge of the truth and knowledge of their Redeemer and great and true shepherd. They will be numbered among his sheep.

l: believers in Samuel's words, The Book of Helaman
s: Believers in Samuel’s words sought Nephi, repented and confessed sins for baptism, then increased after Samuel resisted stones and arrows.

l: unbelievers in Samuel's words, The Book of Helaman
s: A group opposing Samuel grows angry, attributes the Lord’s Spirit to the devil, attacks him, and seeks to bind him.

l: Samuel's words, The Book of Helaman
s: concern the coming of Christ [as a future event] Samuel's words led believers to repentance and baptism, while unbelievers rejected them and attacked Samuel.

l: baptism, The Book of Helaman
s: Baptism was sought by those who believed Samuel's words and came repenting and confessing their sins.

l: miracles, The Book of Helaman
s: Nephi worked miracles among the people, and miracles were also wrought among the people of the Lord.

l: rumors and contentions, The Book of Helaman
s: are_spread_by Satan [across the land] Rumors and contentions were spread across the land by Satan to harden the hearts of the people.

l: tradition, The Book of Helaman
s: is_a wicked tradition [handed down by fathers] The people called the teaching about Christ a wicked tradition handed down by their fathers.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: This document summarizes the first thirty chapters of Third Nephi. Nephi, son of Helaman, leaves Zarahemla and entrusts the records to another Nephi. Signs of the Lord’s birth, a night without darkness and a new star, preserve believers and lead many to repentance, though the Gadianton robbers grow powerful. As people forget the signs and become wicked, the Nephites and converted Lamanites unite under Lachoneus and Gidgiddoni, gather at Zarahemla, repent, fortify themselves, and defeat the robbers led by Giddianhi and Zemnarihah. Peace follows, but pride, inequality, persecution, and secret combinations destroy the government; Nephi nevertheless preaches, performs miracles, and converts some people. In the thirty-fourth year, catastrophic storms, earthquakes, fire, burial, sinking cities, and three days of darkness destroy many wicked people. Jesus Christ speaks to the survivors, calls them to repent, declares that he fulfilled the law of Moses, and teaches sacrifice through a broken heart and contrite spirit. He then appears at the temple in Bountiful, shows the multitude his wounds, gives authority to baptize, and teaches repentance, faith, baptism, humility, mercy, reconciliation, love, prayer, fasting, forgiveness, trust in God, righteous judgment, and obedience. Jesus ministers further by healing the afflicted, blessing children, instituting bread and wine in remembrance of his body and blood, granting the Holy Ghost, praying for unity, and teaching scripture, covenant, gathering, Zion, New Jerusalem, and warnings to the Gentiles. He commands the people to search Isaiah, records Samuel the Lamanite’s prophecy, and gives words concerning the Lord’s refining judgment, tithes, the day of the Lord, and Elijah. Mormon explains that only part of Christ’s teachings is recorded. The disciples establish the church in Christ’s name, baptize and teach, and three are permitted to remain and minister without death. The book closes by warning Gentiles to repent, receive baptism and the Holy Ghost, accept revelation and miracles, and be numbered with the house of Israel.

l: Lehi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Lehi leaves Jerusalem and brings the plates of brass out; his descendants are called the children of Lehi, including Mormon.

l: Lachoneus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Lachoneus, a just chief judge and governor, receives Giddianhi’s threat without fear, gathers the people to repent, pray, and prepare, appoints Gidgiddoni to command the armies, builds fortifications, and with other leaders establishes great peace in the land.

l: Nephi (son of Helaman), The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Nephi, son of Helaman, is a prophet who testifies boldly of repentance and remission of sins through faith on the Lord Jesus Christ. Angels minister to him daily, and he ministers with power: casting out devils and unclean spirits, raising his brother after his death, and performing miracles in the sight of the people. At the commencement of the thirty and third year he preaches repentance and remission of sins and ordains men to baptize those who repent. He later departs Zarahemla, entrusting sacred records and things to his eldest son, Nephi.

l: Nephi (son of Nephi), The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Nephi, eldest son of Nephi (son of Helaman), keeps the records and sacred plates of brass. Seeing the people’s wickedness and threats against believers, he prays mightily to the Lord, receives the Lord’s word, and goes among the people baptizing them unto repentance.

l: Samuel the Lamanite, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Samuel the Lamanite is a prophet and servant of Jesus who testifies to Jesus’ people. Some reject his words about a sign, though it is fulfilled. Commanded to foretell saints rising, appearing, and ministering, he gives a prophecy later fulfilled according to Jesus’s words.

l: the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The Lord is the Son of God and comes among the children of men to fulfill what was made known from the foundation of the world. He declares that he will come into the world, fulfill the words of the holy prophets, and do the will of both the Father and the Son. His work includes bringing again Zion, redeeming Jerusalem and the house of Israel, remembering the covenant and remnant of Israel, and bringing remnants to knowledge of their God who has redeemed them. He works through revelations, prophecy, gifts, tongues, healings, and the power of the Holy Ghost. The Lord delivers his people when they cry for strength and wait for deliverance, amid condemnation of his prophets and threats against his people. He comes to judgment as a swift witness against wrongdoing and oppression, and his justice overtakes those who spurn his doings. Unchanging, he calls people to return, opens heaven’s windows in response to tithes, rebukes the devourer, and spares his jewels. In the end, the proud and wicked are burned up, while those who fear his name receive healing and the wicked become ashes.

l: the Son of God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The Son of God is God of the whole earth, Redeemer, maker, and husband of the woman. The people begin to know he must shortly appear after the sign. His kingdom is associated with those who come unto Jesus Christ as little children. Though his wrath is toward the woman briefly, he gathers her, gives everlasting kindness and mercy, establishes her in righteousness, protects her, and makes attackers fall. He also commands Mormon what to write, testing his people’s faith.

l: the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The Father is the heavenly Father, united with Jesus Christ and the Holy Ghost, who glorifies his name in Jesus and is well pleased with him. From heaven, he directs people to hear Jesus, gives doctrine and commandments through him, and calls all people to repent, believe, and obey. He gives good things to those who ask, receives witnesses of remembrance and obedience, hears prayers offered in Jesus’s name, and gives the Holy Ghost because of Jesus. He sends Jesus to do his will, including being lifted up upon the cross. The Father directs Jesus concerning the twelve disciples, other sheep, and the house of Israel; separates peoples because of iniquity; gives inheritances and promised land; and makes, remembers, and fulfills covenants with the house of Israel. He will bring the gospel, gather dispersed Israel, establish them and Zion, redeem Jerusalem, prepare the way for lost tribes to come to Jesus Christ, and establish the church among those who repent. He blesses believing Gentiles but warns, judges, and executes vengeance on those who refuse repentance. He determines when written things go to the Gentiles, commands scriptures for future generations, shows his works in the church, and brings all things to fulfillment according to his will.

l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Jesus is the Redeemer, Lord, God, beloved Son of the Father, and the light and life of the world. He takes upon himself and is slain for the sins of the world, drinking the bitter cup given by the Father and suffering the Father’s will. Prophets testify that he will come, and after his ascension he manifests himself to the spared people. He appears to a great multitude, identifies himself, gives Nephi and the twelve authority to baptize, promises baptism with fire and the Holy Ghost, and teaches his doctrine. He fulfills the law of Moses in himself, gives commandments, requires repentance, a broken heart, love for enemies, obedience, endurance, and perfection. He teaches prayer, fasting, worship, judgment, seeking the kingdom of God, and hearing and doing his sayings. He heals the sick, afflicted, lame, blind, and deaf, raises a man from the dead, blesses and ministers to children, reveals greater things to them, and shows compassion and mercy. He institutes bread and wine, gives chosen disciples power to give the Holy Ghost, ascends to heaven, and later returns to minister, pray, and teach. He expounds and commands the writing and searching of scriptures, teaches of covenants, gathering, judgments, his future glory, and his judgment of the world. He establishes his gospel and church among the disciples, promises eternal life to those who endure, and commands that the Gentiles repent, come unto him, and be baptized in his name.

l: Satan, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Satan is a person with power over people when they yield to him. He gains possession of their hearts, blinds them, and leads them to reject the doctrine of Christ as foolish and vain. He stirs up iniquity and pride, tempts people to seek power, authority, riches, and vain things, and leads them away from God. His power is linked to people yielding themselves to him, and he desires to sift the multitude as wheat. Watching and praying prevents entering temptation, and he has no power over the three disciples after the change wrought upon their bodies.

l: the people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: A people divided over prophecies see the sign, are astonished, and many convert to the Lord. They receive baptism, remission of sins, and peace, while Gadianton robbers continue causing slaughter.

l: believers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Believers have faith in prophets and their fathers’ tradition, remember Jesus and receive his Spirit. Sorrowful when unbelievers deny the prophecies, they steadfastly await the promised sign. Though threatened with destruction and death, they are preserved when the sign appears.

l: unbelievers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: plan the planned destruction of the believers Unbelievers say that the time for Samuel the Lamanite's words has passed and make a great uproar. They set a day to put believers to death, but when the sign appears many fall to the earth, become as if dead, and fear because of their iniquity and unbelief.

l: Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The Nephites are a people in the land of Zarahemla who possess liberty, property, rights, government, armies, and lands northward and southward. Some dissent and flee to the Gadianton robbers, bringing sorrow. Facing the robbers’ destruction and violence, the Nephites take up arms alongside converted Lamanites, yet suffer afflictions because of iniquity. They gather as one body with families, flocks, herds, provisions, and possessions, repent of all sins, pray to the Lord, build defenses, and prepare for war. Protected through prayer and dependence on the Lord God, they store seven years’ provisions, defeat Giddianhi’s armies, resist Zemnarihah’s siege, capture robbers, and rejoice in deliverance. They believe the holy prophets, know Christ had come through signs and fulfilled prophecy, forsake sins, and serve God diligently. Returning to their lands, they prosper and rebuild cities, but later fall into disputings, pride, persecutions, and iniquity.

l: Lamanites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The Lamanites are a people whose faith and righteousness decline when some rising-generation children, persuaded by Zoramites, join the Gadianton robbers, bringing sorrow, destruction, and violence. Converted Lamanites unite with the Nephites and take up arms against the robbers to protect their lives, families, rights, worship, freedom, and liberty. Some robbers who covenant to keep peace remain Lamanites and receive lands. A few are converted to the true faith, baptized with fire and the Holy Ghost, and remain firm, steadfast, and immovable.

l: Gadianton robbers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The Gadianton robbers are a numerous secret society of robbers who dwell in mountain strongholds and secret places, infest the land, and commit murders, slaughter, death, and carnage. They grow as dissenters and some Lamanites join them, lay waste to cities, and gain advantages through wickedness and divisions among the people of Nephi. Led by Giddianhi, with armies organized in secret places, they threaten the Nephites with utter destruction unless they surrender and join them. They occupy deserted Nephite lands, but their dependence on wilderness food leaves them without provisions and wild game during a siege; they can survive only by plundering, robbing, and murdering. Their armies are defeated with heavy losses and hunger. Most are captured, while the remainder are slain. Prisoners are taught the word of God; those who repent and covenant to murder no more are released to keep the peace, while others are condemned and punished.

l: prophets, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The prophets testify for many years of the Lord’s birth and coming events, and the promised sign is fulfilled. From Samuel onward, they testify of Jesus Christ, including the deaths and destructions at his coming. Wicked people persecute, stone, cast out, and murder prophets because of their testimony; their rejection brings destruction, and the blood of the prophets cries against them. Yet the more righteous part of the people receives the prophets and does not stone them. Many prophets who testify are slain, while their words establish the people as children of the prophets and of the covenant.

l: children of men, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: are_judged_by judgment [according to their works] Men lift Jesus up upon the cross, and the Father will lift men up to stand before Jesus for judgment. Men are also commanded to do the works they have seen Jesus do.

l: Jerusalem, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Jerusalem is a city and land of inheritance. Lehi and those with him were brought out from it by God. Jesus ministered among its people, who saw and were with him. Its waste places will rejoice as the Lord comforts and redeems it; gathered people will receive and inhabit it again, clothed as the holy city.

l: land northward, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The land northward suffers greater destruction than the land southward: tempests, whirlwinds, thunderings, lightnings, and quaking change its whole face, break roads, destroy cities, and slay or carry away many inhabitants.

l: the plates of brass, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The plates of brass are written scriptures said to be fulfilled by the coming of Jesus Christ and by destructions. Readers are told to search them; Jesus expounds them, commands teaching, and wants additional scriptures written.

l: the law of Moses, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The law of Moses is a law containing statutes and judgments, commanded to Moses in Horeb for all Israel. Some wrongly teach that it need no longer be observed, but it must be fulfilled in every whit, without loss of a jot or tittle until all is fulfilled. Jesus did not come to destroy it or the prophets; the law is fulfilled completely in him and has an end in him, while old things are done away and all things become new. Yet it is to be remembered.

l: the scriptures, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Scriptures given by the Father to Jesus for future generations, expounded to a multitude, though some contentiously use them against Moses’s law.

l: the prophecies of the prophets, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The prophecies of the prophets begin to be fulfilled more fully in the ninety and second year. They are fulfilled in the sign, the night without darkness, the new star, and the birth of the Lord.

l: the sign of the Lord's birth, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is a night without darkness [given at the Lord's birth] The sign of the Lord's birth is given as promised: there is no darkness at the going down of the sun, and a new star appears according to the word. The people recognize that the sign has come and that the Lord should be born.

l: the night without darkness, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a sign [of the Lord's birth] The night without darkness is as light as mid-day, and the sun rises the next morning according to its proper order. This fulfills the sign given by the prophets.

l: the birth of the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_signaled_by the sign of the Lord's birth The birth of the Lord is recognized by the people because the night without darkness and the other promised signs occur. The Lord declares that he will come into the world to fulfill all that has been spoken by the holy prophets.

l: remission of sins, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Remission of sins concerns receiving forgiveness through faith in the Lord Jesus Christ, repentance, and baptism with water or in his name, including Gentiles.

l: peace, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: begins_after baptism unto repentance [among the people] Peace was established throughout the land and continued for several years. It ended as disputings, pride, persecution, and iniquity increased.

l: faith, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Faith is a quality whose reality is confirmed when a promised sign is given, leading many to believe and be converted, though it can later diminish through wickedness. It matters because little faith is linked to worry about provision, while sufficient faith enables healing and brings blessing. Faith in Jesus’s words purifies those chosen and those who believe on the disciples’ words. It is also tested: believing what is first received leads to greater things being made manifest, while unbelief causes those greater things to be withheld unto condemnation.

l: repentance, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Repentance is a response to iniquity and a turning from wicked ways, evil doings, wickedness, and abominations. It is required for deliverance, salvation, healing, the kingdom of God, baptism, and receiving the gospel sacrament after unworthiness. Lachoneus teaches the people to repent of all iniquities for deliverance from the Gadianton robbers, and the Nephites later recognize repentance as a reason for their deliverance from everlasting destruction. Nephi preaches repentance and remission of sins, and many are baptized unto repentance. After a great and terrible day, people regret not repenting earlier and are called to repent, return to Jesus Christ, and receive eternal life. Jesus Christ commands all to repent, become as a little child, and seek baptism through those with authority. Those who repent, are baptized in his name, and endure to the end may be filled, held guiltless, and numbered among his people and the house of Israel; those who do not repent are not numbered and may be cut off.

l: iniquity, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Iniquity is wickedness marked by secret and abominable combinations, murders, contention, dissension, and a motive to seek power. It causes fear and gives the Gadianton robbers advantages, while enemies use power and secret combinations in seeking to slay the Nephites. Satan’s influence leads people knowingly and wilfully to rebel against God for power, authority, riches, and worldly things. Even those claiming works in Jesus’s name may be rejected as workers of iniquity. It also separates the twelve disciples from the other tribes of the house of Israel. The wicked secret combinations and their murders are ultimately brought to an end.

l: the people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The people forget and disbelieve signs and wonders, become less astonished by heavenly signs, harden their hearts and blind their minds, then grow increasingly strong in wickedness and abominations despite preaching and prophesying.

l: signs and wonders, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a wonders from heaven The people begin to forget the signs and wonders they had heard and become less astonished at signs or wonders from heaven. They begin to disbelieve all that they had heard and seen.

l: the doctrine of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a foolish and vain thing [in the belief induced among the people] The people are led to believe that the doctrine of Christ is a foolish and vain thing.

l: Nephi (father of Nephi), The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Nephi, father of Nephi and keeper of the records, fails to return to Zarahemla and cannot be found anywhere in the land.

l: Nephi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Nephi is a record keeper who gives a shorter but true account and has charge of the records. Mormon makes his record from Nephi’s engraved record. Nephi comes forth at Jesus Christ’s command, receives authority to baptize, and later brings forth his record, noting omitted saints’ rising and ministering.

l: Zarahemla, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Zarahemla is a great city and land appointed for Nephites to gather with their possessions and defend against enemies; it is later destroyed and burned by fire in judgment, prompting remorse over unrepented brethren.

l: Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Jesus Christ is the Son of God, Redeemer, creator of the heavens and earth, and the light and life of the world. He is with and in the Father from the beginning, existed before the world, and is one with the Father; he is Alpha and Omega. Prophets, including Moses and Samuel, testify of him, and people reckon time from his coming after foretold signs. Men from heaven testify of his death, sufferings, and resurrection. He comes to his own, calls people to repent and come unto him, saves the world from sin, brings redemption, offers eternal life, and extends mercy to all who will come. Those who receive and believe on his name become sons of God. He baptizes the broken heart and contrite spirit with fire and the Holy Ghost. He ministers among people, is praised by the spared people, and teaches prayer. Bread and wine represent his body and blood in the sacrament. He has other sheep beyond this land and Jerusalem, whom he will gather into one fold, and he gathers the house of Israel from the four quarters of the earth. He teaches the fulfillment of the Father’s covenant, the gathering of Israel, redemption of Jerusalem, and matters concerning Gentiles and the gospel. Mercy, justice, and holiness are in him, and his works and miracles should not be denied.

l: the coming of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The coming of Christ is a period marked by a sign from which the Nephites reckon time. It matters because prophets testified of it, its scriptures and prophecies were fulfilled, and many signs showed that Christ had come. Jesus says he came unto his own, who received him not; many who testified were slain.

l: converted Lamanites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Converted Lamanites unite with the Nephites for the safety of their lives, women, and children against the Gadianton robbers. They are numbered among and called Nephites; their curse is removed, their skin becomes white, and their young men and daughters become exceedingly fair.

l: the war between the Gadianton robbers and the people of Nephi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a war [between the robbers and the people of Nephi] The war begins to cause wars and contentions throughout the land and becomes exceedingly sore. The Nephites gain some advantage in the fourteenth year, but the Gadianton robbers gain many advantages in the fifteenth year because of the wickedness, contentions, and dissensions of the people of Nephi.

l: the promised land, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The promised land is an inheritance given by the Father to the house of Israel and the remnant of Jacob. It is the land of Jerusalem, theirs forever. After silence, darkness, trembling, destruction, and the earth standing again, the Father commands Jesus to give it to the people, who will build the New Jerusalem there.

l: destruction, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Destruction is a sword hanging over the Nephites for iniquity, threatening utter ruin before the thirteenth year and smiting by the fifteenth; it is also the destination of the broad way entered by many.

l: Giddianhi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Giddianhi is a robber leader and governor of the secret society of Gadianton. He leads the Gadianton robbers, values their ancient secret works and unconquerable spirit, and demands that Lachoneus surrender the Nephites’ lands and possessions. When refused, he commands war against the Nephites; his armored armies are defeated, and he flees before being overtaken and slain.

l: Gidgiddoni, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Gidgiddoni is a Nephite chief captain, army commander, great prophet, chief judge, and leader. Appointed chief commander, he counsels preparation against robbers. He commands pursuit of Giddianhi’s forces, blocks the robbers’ retreat, and causes them to be cut off. With judge Lachoneus and other leaders, he establishes great peace in the land.

l: God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: God is the Father in heaven, perfect and seated in heaven. He protects and delivers the Nephites when they call on him, and they praise him for preservation from destruction. He gives knowledge unto salvation, knows needs before being asked, sees secret acts and rewards openly, feeds fowls, clothes grass, and sends sun on both evil and good. People are to glorify him through good works, serve him diligently after forsaking sins, and witness repentance through baptism. Though some rebel knowingly, persecuted people may become humble and penitent. He sends a messenger to prepare his way, and at the great and last day all people, kindreds, nations, and tongues stand before him to be judged according to their works.

l: land of the Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a land [claimed by the Nephites and threatened by the robbers] The land of the Nephites is threatened by the Gadianton robbers. The people gather in one place within it to defend themselves.

l: wilderness, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: contains wild game [which becomes scarce] The wilderness was the only place where the robbers could obtain food, but wild game there became scarce. The robbers were consequently about to perish with hunger.

l: fortifications, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a defensive structures [built around the gathered people] Fortifications are built around the gathered people, and their strength is made exceedingly great.

l: armies, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Armies of Nephites and Lamanites guard the people day and night against robbers, prepare for battle, and are commanded by Gidgiddoni.

l: letter from Giddianhi to Lachoneus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Epistle from Giddianhi to Lachoneus praises firmness, demands surrender and alliance, offers safety for joining robbers, and threatens invasion and destruction for refusal.

l: liberty, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a possession [defended by the Nephites] Giddianhi claims that his people are recovering rights and government, while Lachoneus and his people are described as defending their liberty and property.

l: country, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The land has peace, prosperity, and rebuilding until transgression brings inequality, wickedness, and conspirators seeking a king.

l: rights and government, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a possession [claimed by Giddianhi's people] Giddianhi says the robbers seek to recover their rights and government from those who have dissented away from them. He threatens to avenge their alleged wrongs.

l: prayer, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Prayer is an appeal to the Lord for strength and deliverance. Lachoneus leads the people to cry for strength and deliverance from enemies. Jesus commands continual prayer to the Father in his name, in families and for worshippers. The multitude and disciples pray to the Father in Jesus’s name; disciples also pray unceasingly to Jesus, while Jesus prays to the Father.

l: battle against the Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: A great and terrible battle between robber armies and the Nephites begins after the Nephites gather forces, fortify themselves, and prepare weapons and armor under Gidgiddoni. In the sixth month of the nineteenth year, it brings unprecedented slaughter, but the Nephites defeat Giddianhi’s armies and pursue them to the wilderness borders.

l: threatened invasion, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a military attack [by Gadianton robbers against the Nephites] Giddianhi threatens to send his armies against the Nephites on the morrow month if they do not surrender. Lachoneus organizes the people and defenses in response to this threat.

l: Zemnarihah, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Robber leader Zemnarihah causes a siege around the Nephites, commands withdrawal, is captured, and is hanged upon a tree until dead.

l: armies of the Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Nephite armies, provisioned for seven years, pray for protection, confront Giddianhi’s forces, pursue and trap the robbers, and defeat them.

l: siege of the Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Robbers besieged the Nephites to cut them off, but abundant provisions and continual Nephite attacks made the siege fail.

l: slaughter, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a destruction of robbers [by the Nephites] The battle and subsequent pursuit produced great and terrible slaughter. The Nephites also caused great destruction among the robbers by attacking them by night and by day.

l: hanging of Zemnarihah, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a execution [by hanging on a tree] Zemnarihah was captured and hanged upon a tree until he was dead. The tree was then felled, and the Nephites cried that those who sought to slay them through power and secret combinations should likewise be felled.

l: deliverance of the Nephites, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The Nephites defeat Giddianhi’s armies, end Zemnarihah’s siege, and rejoice, crediting deliverance from enemies to repentance and humility.

l: humility, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: contributes_to deliverance of the Nephites [with repentance] The Nephites knew that their humility was a reason they had been delivered from everlasting destruction.

l: righteousness, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_from the Lord [the righteousness of the servants of the Lord] The woman will be established in righteousness, and the righteousness of the Lord's servants is of the Lord.

l: Mormon, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Mormon is a disciple of Jesus Christ, a pure descendant of Lehi, writer, and record keeper called to declare his word. Named after the land of Mormon, he makes a record on plates with his own hands, drawing on earlier accounts and what he has seen. He writes a lesser part of Jesus’s teachings, ends those sayings, and later pauses his account, withholding the three disciples’ names as forbidden while testifying that he has seen them minister among all nations.

l: the church of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The church of Christ is a church established in the land of Mormon by Alma and later to be established among Gentiles who repent and hearken to Jesus Christ’s words. It consists of people who believe and are baptized in Jesus’s name; they receive the Holy Ghost and are united to it. Called in Jesus’s name and built upon his gospel, it receives the Father’s blessing and works for Jesus’s sake. It administers bread and wine and includes prayer among repentant, baptized people. A church built on men’s or the devil’s works ends and is cast into fire. Its disciples face imprisonment but cannot be held.

l: the plates of Nephi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: An engraved record bearing Nephi’s account and most teachings of Jesus; Mormon makes his record from it.

l: record, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Mormon’s record, based on Nephi and written on Nephi’s plates, is a just and true small account spanning Lehi’s departure from Jerusalem to Mormon’s day, containing Mormon’s own observations though many things cannot be written.

l: the house of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The house of Israel is a people descended from Jacob, with some members dwelling at Jerusalem and a remnant of Jacob among them. God has blessed them through mercy and covenanted with them, promising to remember and fulfill that covenant in due time and to bring them to knowledge of their Redeemer, Jesus, and the fulness of the gospel. Though nourished and spared, they would not be gathered and have wickedness and unbelief. Consequently they are scattered across the earth, smitten and afflicted, cast out, trodden under foot, hated, and made a hiss and byword among the Gentiles. The Lord will gather this people from long dispersion and the four quarters of the earth, establish them in Zion, and receive them if they repent and return with full purpose of heart. Those who refuse repentance will be cut off; repentant Gentiles may be numbered among the people of the house of Israel.

l: the remnant of the seed of Joseph, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: A remnant of the seed of Joseph receives mercy and is again brought to knowledge of God; Jacob testified concerning it, and it is addressed as a remnant of its seed.

l: seed of Jacob, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The seed of Jacob is scattered across the earth, then its remnant is gathered by God from the earth’s four quarters.

l: the covenant with the people Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The covenant with the people Israel is made by the Father with all the house of Israel. It matters because the Father remembers and fulfills it by gathering his people, bringing them to knowledge of the fulness of the gospel, and restoring them to their fathers’ lands for inheritance. Its fulfillment begins when these sayings come forth among the Gentiles and proceeds through works from the Gentiles to the seed of the house of Israel. Those who repent and hearken come into it; among robbers, repentance requires a promise to murder no more and brings liberty. In the Father’s due time, the covenant is fulfilled through Israel’s gathering and restoration.

l: capture of the robbers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: results_in preaching the word of God [to imprisoned robbers] The robbers are captured, with none escaping except those who are slain. The prisoners are placed in prison and taught the word of God.

l: gathering of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Gathering of Israel is the Lord’s gathering of the remnant seed of Jacob and dispersed house of Israel from long dispersion across the earth. From east, west, south, and north, they are brought to knowledge of the Lord and to their inherited lands, including Jerusalem and the New Jerusalem, with repentant people assisting.

l: restoration of the house of Jacob, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Restoration of the house of Jacob brings its people to knowledge of the covenant and of Jesus Christ, then gathers the children of Israel to their inherited lands; it begins to be fulfilled as these sayings come to the Gentiles.

l: Lachoneus the younger, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a governor [successor to his father Lachoneus] Lachoneus the younger filled the seat of his father and governed the people in the thirtieth year.

l: people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: A people return to their lands, prosper, establish peace, then divide by riches, learning, pride, and poverty, descend into awful wickedness, rebel against God, and oppose testimonies of Christ.

l: church, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_broken_up all the land [except among a few converted Lamanites] The church began to be broken up because of great inequality and, in the thirtieth year, was broken up throughout the land except among a few converted Lamanites.

l: lawyers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Many lawyers in the land were angered by prophets’ testimony of Christ and nearly all joined kindreds and friends of judges accused of killing prophets.

l: judges, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Judges secretly and unlawfully put prophets and witnesses of Christ to death. Accused of murder, they unite with lawyers, high priests, friends, and kindreds in a covenant to defeat justice, destroy the governor, and establish a king over liberty.

l: high priests, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: enter_into covenant [with judges and lawyers] Some high priests were among those angered by testimony concerning Christ. Almost all the high priests joined with the kindreds of the judges who were to be tried.

l: prophets of the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Prophets of the Lord are heaven-inspired men sent among people to testify boldly of Christ’s redemption, resurrection, death, and sufferings; many testify, then judges secretly seize and kill them unlawfully.

l: riches, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Great riches caused some people to become proud and boastful and contributed to distinctions by rank. Riches also gave some people access to great learning, while poverty left others ignorant.

l: laws, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: are_according_to equity and justice [in the land] The people formed laws according to equity and justice. The law prohibited anyone from being put to death without power from the governor, but judges violated this law.

l: pride, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: cause persecution [among the people] Pride arose among people because of their exceedingly great riches and contributed to boastings, persecutions, inequality, and the breaking up of the church.

l: persecution, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Persecution suffered for Jesus’s name brings blessedness, the kingdom of heaven, joy, and a great heavenly reward.

l: redemption, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Redemption comes by Jesus Christ, who entered the world to bring it; men sent from heaven testified of it.

l: resurrection of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Jesus Christ lays down his life, takes it up again, and men inspired from heaven testify boldly of his resurrection.

l: covenant, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: A covenant, administered by Satan, begins among robbers to keep peace and gain lands, then expands through leaders to oppose righteousness, protect murderers, destroy the governor, and establish a king.

l: justice, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The judges’ unlawful killings led to a complaint and a trial intended to administer justice according to the law. The conspirators united to deliver the guilty from justice.

l: king, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: rule land [with the land subject to kings rather than at liberty] The conspirators covenanted to destroy the governor and establish a king so that the land would no longer be at liberty but would be subject to kings.

l: the people of Nephi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The people of Nephi destroy their government, divide into tribes, and fall into contention and wickedness. Most reject prophets and yield to Satan; only a few turn to the Lord Jesus Christ through Nephi's ministry.

l: chief judge of the land, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The chief judge of the land was murdered on the judgment seat in the thirtieth year.

l: government of the land, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The government of the land was destroyed when the people divided into tribes and when secret combinations undermined its regulations.

l: tribes, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Tribes are family-, kindred-, and friend-based groups whose members appoint chiefs, grow exceedingly great, establish laws and government by their leaders, and maintain some peace through strict rules and agreements not to war. They are also united in hatred against those who entered a covenant to destroy the government.

l: leaders of tribes, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Each tribe appointed a chief or leader over itself. The leaders established the laws and manner of government for their tribes.

l: secret combination, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
