s: A secret combination of friends and kindreds of prophet-murderers, led by Jacob, causes great iniquity, destroys government regulations, then gathers and flees north.

l: Jacob, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Jacob became king of a wicked band, opposed prophets who testified of Jesus, and ordered the band to flee north because enemies were more numerous. He was an ancestor of the house of Israel and later testified concerning a remnant of the seed of Joseph.

l: wicked band, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: A secret-combination group led by Jacob, its king, flees northward to build a kingdom, though less numerous than the tribes, while expecting many dissenters.

l: kingdom of God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The kingdom of God belongs to those who come unto Jesus Christ as little children. It is to be sought first with righteousness, with needed things added to those who do so. Believers who repent, are baptized in Jesus Christ’s name, and become childlike may inherit it. No unclean thing enters; those washed through faith, repentance, and faithfulness to the end enter his rest.

l: the land, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The land was divided among tribes and leaders, and its government was destroyed. Some degree of peace existed in the land despite the people's wickedness.

l: laws, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The tribes were not united in their laws, which were established according to the minds of their chiefs and leaders. They made strict laws against one tribe trespassing against another.

l: angels, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Angels rejoice because of the slain, visit Nephi daily for his faith, and descend amid fire to encircle and minister to little children.

l: the ministry of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_given_an_account_later the people of Nephi who were spared [after Christ manifested himself and showed his body] It includes Christ showing his body to the spared people and ministering to them. An account of this ministry is to be given later.

l: miracles, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: are_wrought_by Jesus Christ Miracles can be wrought by Jesus Christ. The text warns that one who says for gain that no miracle can be wrought by him shall become like unto the son of perdition.

l: Spirit of God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: heals sicknesses and infirmities [through those who were wrought upon by the Spirit] The converted testified that they had been visited by the power and Spirit of God. Those healed or delivered from devils manifested that they had been wrought upon by the Spirit of God.

l: baptism, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Baptism is a testimony before God and the people for those who repent and receive remission of sins. It is performed in water by immersion, in the name of Jesus Christ, with authority given to Nephi and others and exercised by the twelve and disciples. Jesus teaches that believers who humble themselves and repent may be baptized; afterward they may receive bread and wine, be received and ministered to, and be called the church of Christ. Baptism is required for the kingdom of God with repentance and becoming as a little child, and it leads toward remission of sins and salvation when joined with belief and hearkening to Jesus’ words. It precedes the Holy Ghost: after Nephi and those chosen by Jesus were baptized and came out of the water, the Holy Ghost fell upon them. Those with broken hearts and contrite spirits are baptized with fire and the Holy Ghost, which sanctifies them and may enable them to stand spotless before Jesus. The command extends to Gentiles who turn from wicked ways and repent.

l: Jesus's ministry, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_called_by Jesus [for the disciples] The disciples ask that their ministry end after they have lived to the age of man. The three disciples continue their ministry by preaching, baptizing, and uniting believers to the church.

l: contention, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Contention is a spirit of the devil found among disciples, stirring people to angry conflict; Jesus Christ declares it not his doctrine and says it should be done away.

l: murder of the chief judge, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The chief judge of the land was murdered on the judgment seat in the thirtieth year, contributing to the destruction of the government.

l: division into tribes, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The people divided into tribes according to family, kindred, and friends. Each tribe appointed a leader and established its own laws and manner of government.

l: preaching repentance, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Nephi preached repentance and remission of sins through faith on the Lord Jesus Christ. He continued preaching to the people at the commencement of the thirty-third year.

l: the people of the land, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The people earnestly seek a sign amid doubtings and disputations. Following destruction and darkness, they continually mourn, howl, and weep, with some regretting they had not repented. They later hear and witness the sayings and voice, experience silence, and again weep and howl for lost kindred and friends.

l: the sign of darkness, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: concerns darkness for three days [over the face of the land] The sign of darkness was given by prophet Samuel, the Lamanite, and concerned darkness covering the land for three days.

l: darkness for three days, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Darkness for three days follows storm and destruction, covering the land without light; survivors feel its vapor amid trembling and noises. It passes away, and by morning the darkness and disturbances cease.

l: the great storm, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a storm [great and unprecedented in all the land] The great storm arose in the thirty-fourth year, in the first month, on the fourth day, and was unlike any storm previously known in the land.

l: the great and terrible tempest, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a tempest [great and terrible] The great and terrible tempest occurred with terrible thunder, exceedingly sharp lightning, and great destruction, shaking the whole earth as if it would divide asunder.

l: the city of Moroni, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Great city Moroni sank into the sea, where its inhabitants were drowned.

l: the city of Moronihah, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Moronihah, a great city, was covered by earth and replaced by a great mountain after the earth was carried up upon it, prompting people’s later grief and regret over unrepented iniquities and abominations.

l: the great and terrible destruction, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The great and terrible destruction included storms, whirlwinds, thunderings, lightnings, earthquakes, fires, sinking cities, fallen buildings, and widespread deaths. It lasted about three hours before darkness covered the land.

l: the earth, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The earth is a place created by Jesus Christ, inhabited throughout and marked by a voice, destructions, tempests, thunderings, lightnings, and quaking. During three days it trembles and its rocks rend; afterward its tremors cease, it cleaves together again, and stands. It is not covered by Noah’s waters again. The remnant of Israel is scattered upon its face, then gathered from its four quarters, and all its ends see God’s salvation. Its inhabitants are drawn to judgment by books recording their works.
